sections.label: Coroners Act streamlining Bill
sections.summary: The Bill streamlines the Act by making Coroner body-viewing discretionary and empowering the Minister for Law to exempt selected deaths.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In that period, however, through usage, we have received some feedback that some aspects of the Act could be further streamlined, enhanced and allow for greater flexibility.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This Bill seeks to do so in two ways: first, to make viewing of the body by the Coroner discretionary rather than mandatory in all cases; second, to empower the Minister for Law to exempt selected deaths from certain provisions of the Act.

sections.label: Discretionary body-viewing effects
sections.summary: Clause 2 makes Coroner body-viewing discretionary, expediting release of the body to family and saving Police, HSA and Coroner resources.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Clause 2 of the Bill, which makes the body-viewing by the Coroner discretionary, will (a) expedite the release of the body to the family; and (b) save resources for the Police, HSA and the Coroner.

sections.label: New section 17A exemption certificate
sections.summary: New section 17A lets the Minister issue a certificate exempting a death, requiring an outside-Singapore injury, disease or condition and a foreign state request.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The new section 17A proposed provides flexibility for Singapore to accede to requests in appropriate cases, by allowing the Minister to issue a certificate to exempt the death from certain provisions of the Act.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: First, the Minister must be satisfied that the deceased had sustained an injury, contracted a disease or suffered a condition, outside Singapore, that apparently caused the death.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Second, a foreign state must make a request for the Minister's certificate – so it is triggered by the foreign state; not by any individual, but by the foreign state – and give an undertaking regarding the retention or transport of the body, or any other matter, that the Minister may require.

sections.label: Effects of Minister's certificate
sections.summary: If the Minister issues a certificate, no post-mortem examination must be conducted and the body must be released immediately to the foreign state.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: If the Minister issues a certificate, a post-mortem examination must not be conducted and the body must be released immediately to the foreign state.

sections.label: Minister's proposed exemption power
sections.summary: The Minister proposed to vest with himself the power to exempt certain deaths from the Coroners Act's application.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The Minister proposed to vest with him the power to exempt certain deaths from the application of the Coroners Act.

sections.label: Public Prosecutor consent question
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Minister should only use his power after the Public Prosecutor had consented.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Would it not be preferable for the Minister to be only allowed to use his power, as contemplated under this Bill, only after the Public Prosecutor had consented.

sections.label: Minister detention needs Prosecutor consent
sections.summary: The Act requires the Minister to obtain the Public Prosecutor's consent before ordering a detention, as the person may face prosecution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This same person may well be subject to prosecution by the Public Prosecutor, exercising his constitutional powers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: That is why it is provided in the Act that the Minister may only order a detention upon procuring the Public Prosecutor's consent.

sections.label: Coroner body viewing made optional
sections.summary: Clause 2 proposes amending section 12 so that the Coroner's viewing of the body becomes optional.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, it is proposed by clause 2 that section 12 be amended to make the viewing of the body by the Coroner optional.

sections.label: Minister certificate releasing bodies to foreign states
sections.summary: New section 17A lets the Minister issue a certificate releasing a deceased's body to a foreign state, stopping all investigations into the death.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Clause 3 of the Bill will introduce a new section 17A to the Act, to provide that if a foreign state has requested release of the body of a deceased in Singapore, then the Minister can consider issuing such a certificate in two situations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If the Minister sees it fit to issue such a certificate for the release of the body of the deceased, then all investigations into the death must stop.

sections.label: Question on foreign state body release
sections.summary: A Member asks the Minister what circumstances prompted the amendment giving flexibility to release a dead body to a foreign state.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: On the first amendment which is to give the Minister flexibility to issue a certificate for the release of a dead body to a foreign state in certain circumstances, I would like to ask the Minister what were the circumstances that prompted this particular amendment.

sections.label: Coroner need not view body
sections.summary: The Bill introduces a new section 12 so the Coroner need not view the body when making a preliminary investigation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Next, on the dispensing of the need for the Coroner to view the body for preliminary investigation, this Bill introduces a new section 12 such that the Coroner does not have to view the body when making this preliminary investigation.

sections.label: Minister certificate for releasing bodies
sections.summary: New section 17A gives the Minister power to issue a certificate to release a deceased person's body to foreign states in certain cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new section 17A provides the Minister’s power to issue a Minister’s certificate to release the bodies of a deceased person to foreign states in certain cases.

sections.label: Review of identification system records
sections.summary: The process involved examining records and the system's reliability, and no misidentifications were found as far as could be told.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And I think I described the process in some detail earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We looked at that, we looked at the records, we looked at the reliability of that system and, as I said just now, we found that as far as we could tell, there were no misidentifications using this system.

sections.label: Checks before issuing certificate
sections.summary: Section 17A(2) sets out checks the Minister considers before issuing a certificate, including forensic pathologist information and directing police assistance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: On the suggestion that there might be a quick handover, there are steps in section 17A(2) which sets out the different checks that the Minister will have regard to prior to issuing the certificate and this includes looking at information from a forensic pathologist, even directing the forensic pathologist to investigate the apparent cause, to have some degree of satisfaction, and also the Minister may direct the Police to provide any further assistance that a pathologist might require.

sections.label: Amendments allow acceding to requests
sections.summary: The amendments do not guarantee all such requests will be granted but create the possibility of acceding to them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: What these amendments do is not to say that in all such requests they will be granted but it creates the possibility of acceding to these requests when they come in.

sections.label: Public interest considered before certificate
sections.summary: Before issuing the certificate, the question of public interest and whether granting it is appropriate will be judiciously considered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: When deciding whether to issue the certificate in the first place, in other words, before we have to get into a situation where we have to decide what happens when we revoke it, the question as to what is public interest, whether it is appropriate in this case, whether we should be granting the certificate, will be judiciously considered.

sections.label: Revocation considerations and no time limit
sections.summary: No time limit is prescribed for revocation, but the Minister must consider elapsed time, prejudice, practicality, and feasibility of review in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: There could be a scenario where the foreign state, for example, withdraws the request for the certificate or that there is now some other material that is known now, that was not available at that point in time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: There is no time limit prescribed for the revocation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But, obviously, the Minister will have to consider the time elapsed that has gone by, the prejudice, if any, that may have been incurred as a result of the body's movement and whether it is practical in the first place, if the body had already gone back, had undertaken a foreign post-mortem examination and it is not feasible to have that review done in Singapore thereafter.
